newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian ski star Tomba opts for fine for assault.
newsitem.headline: Italian ski star Tomba opts for fine for assault.

text.p: Olympic and world skiing champion Alberto Tomba agreed on Monday to pay a 1.5 million lire ($1,000) fine for an alleged assault on a photographer in lieu of a 20-day jail sentence.

The settlement, reached with an examining judge in the town of Fermo near Italy's Adriatic coast, followed an incident at a discotheque in July 1995 involving a photographer who had snapped the temperamental sportsman with a young woman.
Tomba, who did not attend the hearing, agreed through his lawyer to payment of the fine under a plea-bargaining system.
"I agreed only to close the matter there. I've done nothing wrong," Tomba told Italian news agency ANSA by telephone.
The Alpine skiing champion has been involved in several scrapes with news photographers. Both he and his father Franco have accused Italian media of intrusion.

The photographer involved in the Fermo incident, Guido Picchio, alleged that Tomba snatched the keys from his car ignition and called for help from two bouncers at the club who then took away his film.
He announced plans to appeal against Monday's decision. He has alleged that Tomba also threatened him and improperly flashed a Carabinieri (paramilitary police) card at him.
Tomba, who left the Carabinieri force in March, has denied the photographer's version of events.
